title: Museum St. Anton am Arlberg (Kandahar-Haus)
name: Museum St. Anton am Arlberg (Kandahar-Haus)
kurzbeschreibung: The Museum St. Anton am Arlberg in the historic Kandahar-Haus from 1912: cradle of alpine skiing, Hannes Schneider, and classic alpine cinema.
beschreibung:
Overview

The storied Museum St. Anton am Arlberg (widely known as Kandahar-Haus) is nestled in a picturesque landscaped park above the centre of the world-famous alpine village of St. Anton am Arlberg in the Tiroler Oberland at an altitude of around 1,300 metres. Housed in the heritage-listed Art Nouveau Villa Trier dating from 1912, the building represents the cultural memory of a region celebrated worldwide as the undisputed "cradle of alpine skiing". The museum showcases a fascinating collection chronicling the birth of modern winter sports, the Arlberg technique, and alpine cultural history.

Route & Requirements

The stately villa was built in 1912 by Cologne industrialist Bernhard Trier as a summer residence and served in the winter of 1931 as the film set for the legendary mountain and ski film classic "Der weiße Rausch" by Arnold Fanck starring Hannes Schneider. In 1980, the municipality of St. Anton acquired the historic estate and opened the ski and local heritage museum. The permanent exhibition vividly portrays the bold transformation from a secluded mountain farming village into a world-renowned tourism hotspot: from arduous packhorse trails across the Arlbergpass and the epoch-making construction of the Arlberg Railway (1880–1884) to the foundation of the legendary Ski-Club Arlberg in 1901 – the oldest ski club in the Alps. Special tribute is paid to ski pioneer Hannes Schneider, who revolutionised downhill skiing with his Arlberg-Technik (stem turn and parallel turn), laying the foundation for modern alpine ski sport. Historic wooden skis, traditional clothing, race medals from the legendary Arlberg-Kandahar race, and historic photographs document the evolution of alpine ski equipment.

Visit & Arrival

The Museum St. Anton is open year-round from Sunday to Friday from 10:00 to 18:00 (closed on Saturdays). Admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €6.00, seniors approx. €5.00, children and youths (up to 16 years) free. Admission is free with the regional St. Anton Sommer-Karte. On the ground floor and the delightful veranda, a renowned restaurant invites guests to savour refined Tyrolean cuisine. Getting there by public transport: St. Anton am Arlberg is an international Railjet and express train station of the ÖBB; from the railway station, a walk through the pedestrian zone and the holiday park takes just around 8 minutes to the museum. By car: via the S16 Arlberg expressway, exit St. Anton am Arlberg; parking spaces are located at the signposted car parks in the valley (Terminal West or Terminal Mitte car parks).

Tips

The surrounding museum park with its idyllic mountain stream, Kneipp facility, and children's playground is publicly and freely accessible; the exhibition rooms on the ground floor as well as the restaurant feature step-free access (upper floors accessed via a historic wooden staircase). Combine your museum visit with a walk along the Arlberger Heimatrundweg or stop by the sunny veranda in the afternoon for coffee and homemade apple strudel.
